when: a dragon is due in about a minute
asks: should I back before dragon
drake's in a minute, do I recall
back now or stay for dragon
do I have time to base before drake
say: Shove this wave and recall now so you walk to dragon with items, or stay if you're healthy and your gold buys nothing.
more: A recall started a minute out gets you back in time. One started when the dragon appears means you arrive after the first fight is over.
Unspent gold does nothing in a river fight. The same gold as a finished piece is health or damage you actually bring.
Staying is fine when the trip buys you nothing: you keep the wave and you are already close.
check: Where is your wave, how much health and mana do you have, and how far is your lane from the pit?
breaks: Wrong if the wave is stacked against you and would die at your tower: clear it first, and if that makes you late, give the dragon rather than arrive alone.
basis: pro:Before a spawn, arrive alive and on time

when: you hold enough gold to finish an item or a big component
asks: I've got gold, do I back
can I go buy now
should I recall for my item
I can afford it, base or stay
say: Crash the wave into their tower and recall for the item, or stay one more wave if a cannon wave is arriving.
more: Recalling on a crashed wave means their tower eats your minions while you shop, and the next wave meets you in the middle.
Coming back with a finished piece against someone still on components is the cheapest lead in lane.
One more wave is worth it when it is a big one, but not two: gold in your pocket is not helping you trade.
check: Is your wave big enough to reach their tower, and is a cannon minion in the next wave?
breaks: Wrong if you can't push the wave out: recalling on a wave that sits in the middle hands him a freeze. Trade it down, let it come to your tower, then go.
basis: pro:A lead is not power until it is spent

when: you got a kill in lane in the last 20 seconds
asks: I killed him, back or stay
got the kill, what now
do I recall after the kill
kill in lane, push or base
say: Push the wave into tower, then recall and spend the kill gold, or stay for a plate if you're healthy and their jungler showed elsewhere.
more: The kill only pays if he loses minions too. A wave that dies at his tower while he is dead is the real reward.
If you recall without pushing, he walks back to a wave waiting for him and the lane is close to even again.
A plate is extra gold, but you are usually low after a kill and their jungler knows exactly where you are.
check: How much health do you have left, how big is the wave, and when was their jungler last seen?
breaks: Wrong if you are very low and the wave is slow to push: just recall. Dying after the kill hands the gold straight back.
basis: pro:Kills are not a lead if the farm went the other way

when: your health is low and you hold little gold
asks: I'm low but broke, do I back
low hp, no gold, stay or base
should I recall with nothing to buy
I can't afford anything, do I still back
say: Recall now and accept losing a few minions, or hug your tower and soak experience if the wave is about to crash on you.
more: A few minions are cheaper than a death. Dying gives him gold, costs you a longer trip, and loses the same wave anyway.
If the wave is already arriving at your tower, catching it first and then leaving costs you nothing.
Health is a resource like gold. Coming back full lets you stand next to the wave instead of watching it.
check: Can their laner or jungler reach you under tower, and is the wave coming toward you or away?
breaks: Wrong if they can dive you where you stand: do not wait for the wave, leave now. With Teleport you lose almost nothing by going early.
basis: written

when: your lane opponent's items just changed
asks: he just backed, do I back too
enemy recalled, what do I do
he's got a new item, should I base
he went to buy, stay or go
say: Match the recall once your wave is pushed so you fight on even items, or take plates first if you're healthy and have little gold.
more: He comes back with new items and full health. If you stay on old ones, the next trade goes his way even if the last did not.
While he is gone the tower is undefended, so plates are free gold, but only for as long as he takes to walk back.
Pushing first is what makes either choice work: he returns to minions dying at his tower.
check: How much gold do you hold, how healthy are you, and is your wave near his tower?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler has not shown: you are alone and pushed up with their laner on his way back. Take one wave of plates at most, then leave.
basis: pro:Their jungler or carry in base is your window

when: between 6:45 and 7:30
asks: should I back before grubs
grubs soon, recall now?
do I base for grubs
when do I reset for grubs
say: Recall in the next half minute so you're back topside with items for grubs at eight, or keep farming if your team's giving them.
more: Grubs are one window that does not come back, so the team that is on the map with items at eight o'clock usually takes them.
A recall now costs a wave at most. A recall at eight means their side starts the pit while you are in the shop.
If your team is clearly not going, your gold and experience from the wave are worth more than walking up to watch.
check: Is your wave pushed enough to leave, and are your jungler and nearest laner planning to go?
breaks: Wrong if a huge wave is about to hit your tower: catch it, and send the players who are already free. Losing a full wave for a late arrival is a bad trade.
basis: rule

when: after 20:00 and Baron is alive
asks: should we back before baron
do I recall before we go baron
baron's up, buy first?
I've got gold, base before baron?
say: Recall together now and spend before you walk to Baron, or stay and start it if their jungler just died.
more: Baron takes a while and the fight around it is the biggest of the game. Walking in with unspent gold is choosing to be weaker.
Recalling as a group matters as much as recalling at all. One player in base while four stand near the pit is a fight you start short.
If their jungler is dead the maths changes: nobody can steal it, so speed beats items.
check: How much gold are you and your carries holding, and are the side waves pushed before you leave?
breaks: Wrong if the enemy is already standing in the pit area: a recall now gives them the vision and maybe the Baron. Hold the river and send only the lowest player back.
basis: pro:A lead is not power until it is spent

when: two or more enemies died in the last 20 seconds
asks: we won the fight, back or push
do I recall after that fight
I'm low after the fight, base?
fight's over, what do I do
say: Take the nearest tower or objective while they're dead, then recall together, or recall first if you're too low to survive a respawn.
more: Kills are a timer. For as long as they are dead something on the map is undefended, and that is what the fight was for.
Recalling straight away turns a won fight into a small gold lead and nothing else.
If you are nearly dead, the first enemy back kills you and undoes it. Then the right order is base, buy, and come back for the next thing.
check: How long are their death timers, what is closest to you, and how much health does your team have?
breaks: Wrong if the survivors include their best wave clearer and you have no minions with you: you cannot take a tower without a wave. Take camps or vision, then reset.
basis: pro:After a won fight, the waves decide whether you got paid

when: you hold enough unspent gold for a full item
asks: I have a ton of gold, do I back
should I go spend
I'm sitting on gold, base now?
is it worth recalling just to buy
say: You're carrying a full item's worth of gold, so recall after this wave, or stay only if an objective fight starts in seconds.
more: A full item is the biggest single jump in strength you get. Carrying it around unspent means fighting a whole item down for no reason.
The scoreboard shows you ahead, but the real gap is only what is in your inventory.
The one reason to wait is a fight that is already starting. Leaving then costs your team a player at the worst moment.
check: Is anything spawning in the next minute, and is the wave you are on safe to leave?
breaks: Wrong if an objective is about to spawn and you would miss it: fight first on what you have, then recall the moment it is settled.
basis: pro:A lead is not power until it is spent

when: your lane opponent is dead
asks: he's dead, do I back now
enemy laner died, recall or push
should I base while he's dead
he's dead, free recall?
say: Shove the wave under their tower and recall so you lose nothing, or stay and hit plates if you're healthy with little to buy.
more: His death timer is the cheapest recall you will ever get: push, leave, and you are both back in lane at about the same time.
The difference is that you have new items and he has lost a wave to his own tower.
Plates are better when the shop has nothing for you, but they keep you pushed up when he and his jungler return.
check: How long is his respawn, how much gold do you hold, and where was their jungler last seen?
breaks: Wrong if their jungler caused the death and is still nearby and healthy: do not sit at their tower. Push from range, then leave.

asks: when do I back as support
should I recall with my adc
do I base now or stay with him
can I leave lane to buy
say: Recall when your carry does so the lane stays two against two, or go alone right after the wave crashes into their tower.
more: A carry alone against two players loses minions or dies, so the cost of your recall is paid by him.
Recalling together keeps both of you on the same item and health timing for the next trade.
A crashed wave is the one safe moment to go alone: their minions are far away and he can stand back until you return.
check: Where is the wave, how healthy is your carry, and do you have wards left to place?
breaks: Wrong if their duo is strong enough to dive him: do not leave him alone at all. Wait, or tell him to back with you.
basis: written

asks: everyone backed, do I stay
team's all in base, what do I do
am I ok to stay out alone
they all recalled, should I too
say: Recall with them so you're back on the map together, or catch one safe wave near your tower first if no enemy is missing.
more: Recalls that happen at different times leave your team a player short for a long stretch, first you, then them.
While four of yours are in base, you are the only target on the map and the enemy knows it.
A wave close to your own tower is usually safe to take first. One wave, not three.
check: How many enemies can you see on the map right now, and how far from your tower is the wave?
breaks: Wrong if an objective is up and the enemy is alive near it: you cannot hold it alone. Give it, recall, and come back with everyone.
basis: pro:Their jungler or carry in base is your window

when: you have Teleport
asks: should I tp back to lane
do I use teleport after backing
back and tp or walk
is it worth teleporting for the wave
say: Recall and Teleport back if a big wave would die at your tower, or walk and keep it if an objective spawns soon.
more: Teleport to lane buys back a wave you would otherwise lose. That is real gold and experience, and it keeps you level.
The price is that it is unavailable for the next fight. If grubs or a dragon are close, an extra player there is worth more than one wave.
Walking back is fine when the wave is pushed away from you, because you lose little anyway.
check: Is Teleport actually ready, how big is the wave heading to your tower, and what spawns next?
breaks: Wrong if their laner still has Teleport and you just used yours for a few minions: he gets the extra player at the next objective. Count the wave before you press it.
basis: pro:Teleport decides who has the extra player

when: you trail your lane opponent in CS and items
asks: I'm behind, what do I buy
do I back for a small item or wait
should I save up or buy now
I'm losing lane, base now?
say: Buy the cheap piece that helps you survive lane now, or wait one more wave if that finishes a real component.
more: When you are behind, the goal of a recall is to stop the bleeding: something defensive or sustaining now beats a bigger item later.
Gold counts only once it is in an item. Saving while losing every trade means you never reach the item at all.
Waiting a wave is right when you are close to a proper component and the wave is safe to take.
check: What is he building, is the next wave safe to farm, and how close are you to the next component?
breaks: Wrong if you are healthy and the wave is frozen near your tower: stay and farm it. A recall there gives up the one safe place you have.
basis: pro:Early on, a level is worth more than a little gold

asks: can I back right now
is it safe to recall late game
I need to buy, can I leave
do I have time to base
say: Recall right after you push a wave past the river, or stay grouped if Baron or Elder is up and they're all alive.
more: Late in the game a recall is a long stretch where your team is four. A pushed wave is what buys that time safely.
With waves pushing out, the enemy has to answer minions before they can force anything.
If a big objective is alive and they are all alive, your absence is the opening they are waiting for.
check: Are the waves pushing toward them, is Baron or Elder alive, and is every enemy accounted for?
breaks: Wrong if you are the only one with gold to spend and the team will not wait: tell them, back off together to a tower, and go from there.
basis: pro:Push the side waves before you posture at Baron

when: before 5:00
asks: when should I take my first back
when do I first recall
is it too early to back
how long do I stay in lane first
say: First recall after you crash a big wave with enough for a real component, or earlier if you're too low to trade.
more: The first recall sets the timing for the whole lane. Leaving on a crashed wave means you lose almost nothing.
Coming back with a real component rather than scraps is what lets you take the next trade.
Health comes first, though. If you cannot stand near the minions, you are already losing the wave by staying.
check: How much gold do you have, how big is your wave, and how much health is left?
breaks: Wrong if he recalls first on a good wave: do not stay stubbornly on old items. Push what you can and match him.
basis: written

when: your team took a dragon in the last 20 seconds
asks: we got dragon, do I back
drake's done, recall now?
after dragon, base or push
dragon's ours, what next
say: Recall now while the next dragon is five minutes off, or push the nearest wave first if you're healthy and nobody's low.
more: Right after an objective is the quietest moment on that side of the map, so it is the cheapest time to shop.
The next dragon is five minutes away. Recalling now leaves you plenty of time to farm and still be early for it.
Pushing a wave first is a bonus when you are healthy, because the enemy is often recalling too.
check: How low is your team, where are the nearest waves, and is anything up on the top side?
breaks: Wrong if the enemy answered on the top side while you took dragon: someone healthy has to go and clear that wave before it costs a tower.

when: a dragon is due in under a minute
asks: what do I do with my wave before dragon
do I push before drake
dragon's coming, shove or hold
wave before dragon?
say: Shove your wave into their tower now and walk over first, or stay and farm if you can't push it in time.
more: Whoever clears their wave first gets to walk into the river first. That is decided half a minute before the dragon appears.
With your wave at their tower, their laner chooses between minions and following you, and both cost him.
If you cannot push, leaving anyway just loses the wave and gets you there late. Tell your team and keep the farm.
check: Can you actually clear this wave quickly, and is their laner already walking away from it?
breaks: Wrong if pushing means standing in front of their whole lane with no ward: thin the wave from range and accept arriving second rather than dying before the spawn.
basis: pro:The lane that pushes first moves first

asks: how do I set up my wave to back
what do I do with the wave before recalling
how do I recall without losing cs
wave's in the middle, can I back
say: Push the wave all the way into their tower and recall as it lands, or let it crash on yours and back after.
more: A wave that dies at their tower resets the lane. The next two waves meet in the middle while you are walking back.
A wave left in the middle is the worst case: he can hold it there and you lose minions and experience getting back to it.
If you cannot out-push him, the mirror works too: farm the wave at your own tower, then leave once it is gone.
check: How many minions does each side have, and is another enemy wave about to arrive?
breaks: Wrong if you are too low to stand in the wave at all: just go. Losing the wave beats losing the wave and your life.
basis: written

asks: which wave do I catch
where do I farm now
which lane should I go get
what wave is mine
say: Catch the side wave on the same side as the next objective, or the other one if it's about to hit your tower.
more: Pushing the wave nearest the next objective means you finish farming already close to where the fight will be.
That wave then pushes into them just as the objective spawns, so someone on their team has to leave to answer it.
A wave dying at your tower is gold lost for certain, so it wins the tie if you can get there and back in time.
check: Which objective spawns next, where are the side waves, and how many enemies can you see?
breaks: Wrong if the wave is past the river with enemies missing: that is how carries get picked. Wait for it to come to your half or go with a teammate.
basis: written

asks: my laner left, do I push
he's roaming, shove or follow
he's gone, what do I do with the wave
enemy mid's missing, push or follow
say: Shove the wave into his tower so he loses minions and plates, or follow if your wave is already pushed and you'd arrive first.
more: Every wave that dies at his tower while he is away is gold and experience he never gets back. It is a guaranteed punishment.
Following is a gamble on arriving in time. It pays when you leave from a pushed wave and take the shorter path.
Either way, tell the lane he is heading for. A warning costs nothing and often saves the kill.
check: Is your wave already at his tower, which way did he go, and can the lane he is going to step back?
breaks: Wrong if he left to join a fight at an objective that decides the game: minions do not matter then. Go, even if it costs the wave.
basis: pro:The lane that pushes first moves first

when: an objective is due in about two minutes
asks: how do I set up waves for dragon
what do I do with side lane before the objective
how early do I push for drake
waves before objective?
say: Start a slow push on the far side lane now so it lands at the spawn, or just fast shove mid if time's short.
more: A slow push builds a big wave that reaches their tower on its own later, right when you want them distracted.
When it arrives, one of them leaves the objective to stop it, or they lose tower health for free.
Mid is the fallback because it is the shortest lane: a quick clear there still lets your team walk to river first.
check: Which side is the next objective on, how do the side waves look, and who on your team clears fastest?
breaks: Wrong if you set the push up and then stay to watch it: the point is that the wave works without you. Leave it and be at the objective.
basis: pro:A pushed side wave pulls a carry away from the pit

asks: who should be mid right now
do I stay mid or go side
should I hold mid wave
is mid my lane now
say: Hold mid if you clear waves fastest, since mid reaches both rivers, or take a side lane if a stronger wave clearer is there.
more: Mid is the lane closest to both objectives, so the player who clears it quickly decides who moves first.
A fragile carry also farms most safely in mid, because the lane is short and the tower is close.
Two farmers in one lane is wasted gold. If someone better suited is there, a side wave is yours.
check: Who else is standing in mid, and can you clear a full wave before the enemy does?
breaks: Wrong if you are a slow clearer holding mid against a fast one: you will be stuck under tower. Swap with a teammate and take the side lane.
basis: pro:The lane that pushes first moves first

when: after 20:00 and Baron is alive
asks: what do we do with waves before baron
do I push side before baron
waves or baron first
should I go bot before we baron
say: Push both side waves past river before you walk to Baron, or only the far one if there's no time for both.
more: With waves pushing in, they must send someone to clear or lose towers while you stand at the pit.
If they send a player away, you have a numbers edge at Baron without getting a kill.
The wave on the far side from Baron matters most, because answering it is the longest walk away from the pit.
check: Where are all three waves, and how many enemies show up to answer the far one?
breaks: Wrong if pushing the far wave means going alone past river with enemies missing: take it only to the river line, then regroup.
basis: pro:Push the side waves before you posture at Baron

when: your team got two or more kills in the last 20 seconds
asks: we won, do I chase or farm
should I go get the wave after the fight
they're running, chase?
fight's won, wave or kills
say: Leave the chase and catch the big side wave while the others hit a tower, or stay if your damage is needed for it.
more: Fights pull everyone to one spot, so the side waves pile up. Someone has to collect them or they die at your tower.
If all of you chase, the enemy respawns onto waves pushed into your side and has lost very little.
The player who leaves should be the one least needed to hit the tower, often whoever is lowest.
check: Where are the side waves, who on your team is hitting the tower, and how long are their death timers?
breaks: Wrong if the runner is one hit from dying and cannot escape: finish it, then go. A long chase through dark jungle is the part to skip.
basis: pro:After a won fight, the waves decide whether you got paid

when: an allied laner is dead
asks: should I cover his lane
top died, do I take his wave
do I catch the wave for him
he's dead, who gets the minions
say: Catch the wave at his tower so it isn't lost, or leave it if he respawns in time or you'd miss an objective.
more: Minions that die to the tower are gold nobody gets, and the tower takes damage while the lane is empty.
Holding the wave also keeps it from pushing back out, so he returns to minions near his tower.
It is still his lane. Take what would be lost, then leave it to him.
check: How long is his respawn, how big is the wave, and what does your own lane or clear lose while you are away?
breaks: Wrong if the enemy who killed him is still there, healthy and ahead: you are walking into the same fight. Give the wave.

when: you lead your lane opponent in level or items
asks: I'm ahead, freeze or push
should I shove or hold the wave
do I keep the wave here
winning lane, what do I do with the wave
say: Hold the wave near your tower to starve him while nothing's spawning, or shove and move if an objective is under a minute away.
more: A wave held on your side makes him walk far from his tower to farm, where your lead kills him or keeps him off the minions.
That widens the gap without any risk, which is what you want when there is nothing else to take.
The moment an objective is close, a lead sitting in lane is wasted. Push, and bring it to the fight.
check: Where is the wave right now, and when was their jungler last seen?
breaks: Wrong if your team is losing everywhere else: a private lead in a held lane does not help them. Push, take plates, and move.

when: a dragon or the grubs are due within 30 seconds
asks: wave's at my tower but they're doing dragon
do I leave this wave for the fight
farm this or go help
big wave here, do I go
say: Go if your team's already there and you make the numbers even, or take the wave if you'd arrive after it's decided.
more: What matters at an objective is how many bodies each side brings at the moment it is fought.
If you are the player who evens it out, the wave is the price and it is worth paying.
If you would arrive late, you lose the wave and change nothing. Then the wave is the better half of a bad situation.
check: How many of each team are near the pit, and how long is your walk?
breaks: Wrong if you have Teleport ready: take the wave and Teleport in when it starts. Then you get both.
basis: pro:Count who can actually arrive before contesting

when: your team trails in kills and towers
asks: we're losing, where do I farm
where can I safely get cs
which waves are safe when behind
I need farm but we're behind
say: Farm waves on your side of the river and your own camps, or step further only when you see four enemies elsewhere.
more: When you are behind, the enemy has more of the map lit up than you, so anything past the river is a guess.
Waves come to you eventually. Taking them on your half costs a little time and none of your life.
Seeing most of their team somewhere else is the only real permission to push further.
check: How many enemies can you see, and are your outer towers still standing on that side?
breaks: Wrong if staying back means their big wave takes an inhibitor tower: go and clear that one with a teammate, even if it is risky.

do we swap to mid now
where does adc farm after laning
lane's over, where do I go
say: Move to mid, where the lane's short and safe for a carry, or stay bot one more wave if dragon spawns soon.
more: Once an outer tower is gone, that side lane gets long and dangerous. Mid keeps a carry close to a tower and to both rivers.
The solo laners are better at surviving alone in a long lane, so they take the sides.
The exception is a dragon about to spawn: staying bot side keeps you next to it.
check: Which towers are down, who is in mid right now, and when is the next dragon?
breaks: Wrong if your mid laner refuses to leave: do not split the wave between you. Take the side wave only while it is on your half, and ask for the swap.

asks: can I roam now
do I push before I roam
should I leave lane to help
wave first or go now
say: Push the wave in before you leave so you lose nothing, or skip the roam if you can't clear it quickly.
more: A roam from a pushed wave is close to free: their tower takes the minions and the next wave meets yours in the middle.
A roam from a wave pushing into you costs minions, experience and sometimes plates, whether or not the play works.
It also gives you the head start. Your opponent has to clear before he can follow.
check: Where is the wave, and is there actually a target in the lane you want to visit?
breaks: Wrong if a fight is already happening right next to you: go now and pay the wave. A fight in progress does not wait for your minions.
basis: pro:The lane that pushes first moves first

when: the enemy team took Baron in the last couple of minutes
asks: they have baron, how do I clear
how do we defend baron push
what do I do with waves vs baron
they got baron, now what
say: Meet each empowered wave early from tower range and clear it, or give the outer tower if clearing means standing in their whole team.
more: The buff makes their minions the threat. Kill the minions and the champions have nothing to siege with.
The buff runs out, so every wave you clear without dying is time taken off it.
An outer tower is a fair price for not dying. A death under Baron usually costs the inhibitor behind it as well.
check: Which lanes are they pushing, who on your team clears waves best, and how many of them are in each lane?
breaks: Wrong if they split into two lanes and nobody answers the second: one good wave clearer has to go there alone and clear from the tower.

when: a dragon is due in about a minute
asks: what do I do before dragon
dragon in a minute, what's the plan
how do we get this drake
set up for dragon?
say: With a minute left, push your wave, buy, and be in river first, or give it if two teammates are dead or in base.
more: The minute before the spawn decides most dragons: who pushed, who shopped, and who is standing in the river.
Arriving first lets your team place wards and makes them walk in through places they cannot see.
If you are two players short, there is no setup that fixes it. Decide early to give it and you lose only the dragon.
check: Who on your team is alive and on the map, and are the mid and bot waves pushed?
breaks: Wrong if it would be their third dragon: that one is worth showing up for even in a poor state, because the next gives them soul.

should bot rotate for grubs
grubs are up, do I leave lane
do I help top side
say: Stay bot and take plates while they send people to grubs, or send only your support up if your wave is already crashed.
more: Grubs are on the far side of the map from you. The walk there and back costs a carry several waves and leaves the tower open.
If they move players up and you stay, plates and maybe the tower are your payment for the grubs.
A support leaving on a crashed wave is the cheap way to add a body, because the carry can stand back and farm safely.
check: Did their bot lane leave, where is your wave, and can your carry be dived if left alone?
breaks: Wrong if their bot lane stays and is stronger than you two against two: do not push for plates. Hold the wave and give nothing.

do I leave lane for grubs
grubs now or stay in lane
team's on grubs, do I go
say: Push your wave first, then join grubs so their laner must choose, or stay on the wave if he's shoving you under tower.
more: You are the closest lanes to the pit, so whichever of you arrives first usually decides it.
Leaving from a pushed wave costs nothing. Leaving a wave at your tower costs minions and plates for a share of the grubs.
A partial take is still fine. Grubs do not have to be all or nothing.
check: Where is your wave, is their laner still in lane, and how many of each team are at the pit?
breaks: Wrong if your jungler is already fighting there and losing: go now and skip the wave. A lost jungler costs more than minions.

say: Swap to the sweeper once your support item places wards, or keep the yellow trinket if your team has no other vision.
more: When your support item starts holding wards, you have enough of your own, and removing theirs becomes the more valuable job.
Clearing a ward before a gank or an objective is often what makes the play work.
If you swap too early, the lane has no ward at all for a while. That is the risk.

say: Take the sweeper if you're the one walking into brushes first, or the blue trinket if you're a backline carry who shouldn't facecheck.
more: The blue trinket checks a spot from a long way off, so a carry never has to walk into the dark to see it.
The sweeper is for the players at the front, who clear wards before an objective or a flank.
The yellow trinket loses value once supports and junglers are covering the warding.
check: Are you usually at the front or the back of your team, and who else is already sweeping?
breaks: Wrong if nobody on your team is placing wards at all: keep the yellow one. Some vision beats the ideal trinket.
